questions.stem: Find the part of the sentence that has a grammatical error: (A) She is / (B) one of the / (C) most talented singer / (D) in the country.
questions.explanation: After 'one of the', a plural noun is required. 'singer' should be 'singers'. Correct: 'one of the most talented singers in the country'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Neither the students / (B) nor the teacher / (C) were present / (D) in the class.
questions.explanation: With 'Neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it ('teacher', singular). Use 'was present', not 'were present'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The committee / (B) have decided / (C) to postpone / (D) the meeting.
questions.explanation: In formal/standard English (especially in Indian exams), collective nouns like 'committee' take a singular verb. It should be 'has decided', not 'have decided'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) He is / (B) more intelligent / (C) than / (D) any student in the class.
questions.explanation: 'He' is one of the students, so comparing him to 'any student' includes himself. Correct: 'any other student in the class'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) I had / (B) went to the / (C) market / (D) yesterday.
questions.explanation: 'Had went' is incorrect. 'had' (auxiliary) must be followed by a past participle. The past participle of 'go' is 'gone'. Correct: 'I had gone to the market'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The news / (B) are shocking / (C) and everyone / (D) is disturbed.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun that takes a singular verb. 'are shocking' should be 'is shocking'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Each of / (B) the boys / (C) have brought / (D) their own lunch.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is always singular and requires a singular verb. 'have brought' should be 'has brought'. (Note: 'their own lunch' is acceptable with 'each' in modern usage.)
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The two boys / (B) fought with / (C) one another / (D) during the game.
questions.explanation: 'One another' is used for three or more people. For exactly two people, use 'each other'. Correct: 'fought with each other'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) He told / (B) that he / (C) will come / (D) the next day.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, when the reporting verb 'told' is in the past tense, 'will' must change to 'would'. Correct: 'He told that he would come the next day'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The police / (B) has arrested / (C) three suspects / (D) in the case.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural collective noun and always takes a plural verb. 'has arrested' should be 'have arrested'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) No sooner did / (B) he enter the room / (C) when everyone / (D) stood up.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner…than' is the correct correlative conjunction pair. 'when' should be replaced with 'than'. Correct: 'No sooner did he enter the room than everyone stood up'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) She requested / (B) him to kindly / (C) help her with / (D) the assignment.
questions.explanation: 'Kindly' should not be placed between 'to' and the verb (splitting the infinitive awkwardly in formal usage). More critically, in SSC grammar, 'requested him to kindly' is flagged because 'requested' already implies politeness; 'kindly' is redundant. Standard correction: 'requested him to help her'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Despite of / (B) his best efforts, / (C) he could not / (D) solve the problem.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' does not take 'of'. The correct form is simply 'Despite'. Alternatively use 'In spite of'. Correct: 'Despite his best efforts...'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) He is / (B) too tired / (C) to not / (D) work any further.
questions.explanation: 'Too…to' already carries a negative meaning (he is too tired to work). Adding 'not' creates a double negative, making the meaning opposite. Correct: 'He is too tired to work any further'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Mathematics / (B) are a / (C) compulsory subject / (D) in this school.
questions.explanation: Names of subjects ending in '-ics' (Mathematics, Physics, Economics) are treated as singular nouns. 'are a' should be 'is a'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) I prefer / (B) coffee than / (C) tea in the / (D) morning.
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' is always followed by 'to', not 'than'. Correct: 'I prefer coffee to tea in the morning'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The jury / (B) were divided / (C) in their / (D) opinion.
questions.explanation: When members of a collective noun act as individuals (here, each juror has a separate opinion), the plural verb is actually correct in British English. However, in SSC exam conventions, 'jury' acting as a unit takes singular. With 'divided…in their opinion' (showing individual views), 'were divided' is acceptable. The true error is in (C): the correct preposition is 'in' or 'on' their opinion — both can be argued. In standard SSC marking, (B) 'were' should be 'was' (treating jury as a single body).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) If I was you / (B) I would / (C) not have / (D) accepted the offer.
questions.explanation: In hypothetical or contrary-to-fact conditions using 'if', use the subjunctive 'were', not 'was'. Correct: 'If I were you...'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) He works / (B) harder than / (C) any other / (D) members of his team.
questions.explanation: 'Any other' is followed by a singular noun (comparing one person to each other individual). 'members' (plural) should be 'member'. Correct: 'any other member of his team'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The manager / (B) along with his assistants / (C) have attended / (D) the seminar.
questions.explanation: When the main subject 'manager' is followed by a parenthetical phrase ('along with his assistants'), the verb agrees with the main subject, which is singular. 'have attended' should be 'has attended'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Scarcely had / (B) the match begun / (C) than it / (D) started raining.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely…when' is the correct correlative pair (like 'Hardly…when'). 'than' should be 'when'. Correct: 'Scarcely had the match begun when it started raining'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) The number of / (B) students absent / (C) today are / (D) surprisingly high.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb (compare: 'a number of' takes plural). Correct: 'The number of students absent today is surprisingly high'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) It is / (B) high time / (C) we act / (D) on this matter.
questions.explanation: After 'It is high time', the verb must be in the past subjunctive form. 'act' should be 'acted'. Correct: 'It is high time we acted on this matter'.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) Five hundred rupees / (B) are not / (C) a big amount / (D) for such a meal.
questions.explanation: When a sum of money, distance, or period of time is treated as a single unit, it takes a singular verb. 'are not' should be 'is not'. Correct: 'Five hundred rupees is not a big amount…'
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Find the error: (A) He is one of / (B) those leaders who / (C) has always stood / (D) for the truth.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'those leaders' (plural antecedent). The verb must be plural. 'has always stood' should be 'have always stood'. Correct: '…those leaders who have always stood for the truth'.
questions.subject: English
